Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known. In the captured implementation the recovering replica also raises its own record's vbal to the newly made ballot before it builds its PrepareReply, so the resolution's running maximum starts above any value that other replicas accepted at older vbals; the direct checks for claim C1-recovery-adopts-committed-vector confirmed in scope that this lets a recovery commit a NOOP vector for an instance another replica already holds as COMMITTED with a real command, and that the recoverer's Commit broadcast does not repair the disagreement. The same masking holds when the recovering replica is the replica the deployment promoted to leader (IsLeader true, so makeBallot raises the new ballot past maxRecvBallot): the promoted-variant check for claim C6-recovery-ignores-committed-reply-when-promoted confirmed in scope that the committed reply is still skipped and the NOOP vector committed, and the accept handler's own rejection branch for a higher-ballot AcceptReply is unreachable because the ballot-equality gate returns first (claim C7-accept-reply-higher-ballot-is-a-rejection, confirmed in scope), so a rejected round waits for the timeout-driven recovery.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo. Progress when a round is rejected does not come from the handlers: the direct check for claim C8-timeout-enqueues-blocked-instance confirmed that the executor's per-row timeout enqueues the blocked instance for recovery after roughly twelve seconds of wall clock, so a stalled row is recovered by the timeout path rather than by a rejection signal.

open_details: handlePreAccept's status >= ACCEPTED branch stores the incoming command in InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler uses preAccept.Replica (S9-handlePreAccept). Source review of every status-advancing path found no state with Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil: acceptors keep Status NONE, the leader-side accept/commit paths copy commands, and the only nil-Cmds records are fresh defaults with Status NONE. The wrong-slot write is therefore unreachable while acceptors do not record acceptance; the unprotected premise is whether handleAccept is required to record ACCEPTED (S11-handleAccept, S12-handleAcceptReply, S13-handleCommit).

handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal but never records an ACCEPTED status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE; the >= ACCEPTED guards in handlePreAccept and findPreAcceptConflicts therefore only ever see COMMITTED on non-leaders (S11-handleAccept, S9-handlePreAccept, S17-find-conflicts).

handlePrepareReply's sub-cases 3 and 4 carry textually identical guards, so sub-case 3 always wins and sub-case 4 never runs; bcastTryPreAccept is called only from sub-case 4, so handleTryPreAccept, findPreAcceptConflicts, handleTryPreAcceptReply and the possibleQuorum/deferMap machinery are unreachable dead code, and a recovery with weaker pre-accept support takes sub-case 5, which restarts phase 1 with the recovered value (a more conservative path) (S15-handlePrepareReply, S16-handleTryPreAccept, S17-find-conflicts, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply).

handleTryPreAcceptReply's defer-cycle guard counts lb.possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId] inside a loop over q, so the count can only be 0 or N and never equals N/2; the counting error has no reachable consequence because the handler is reachable only from the dead sub-case 4 (S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply).

recordInstanceMetadata writes bal at [0:4) and then vbal into the same bytes, with Status at byte [4] and Seq at [5:9); the direct check for claim C2-durable-record-preserves-written-fields confirmed in scope that the produced record carries vbal at offset 0 and no bal value, so the ballot context the function writes is not recoverable from the layout. No reader of the format exists in the snapshot and run.go passes durable = false, so the consequence is bounded to any future or external reader (S19-durable-record, S24-runReplica-epaxos).
the transconf branch inside Exec.strongconnect computes state.Conflict but performs no action, and run.go passes transconf = false (S20-exec, S24-runReplica-epaxos).

the N<=3 with Thrifty configuration skips the fast-path attribute-equality check while still committing at preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 = 1. The committed vector is the merge of the leader's own and the counted replies' (seq,deps) (mergeAttributes, installed into the bookkeeping before the branch choice), so the exemption does not publish the leader's own proposal vector; what it removes is the requirement that every counted reply already equal that merged vector, which is the step that otherwise either forces agreement or triggers the accept round that puts the merged vector on a majority. With exactly one counted peer the merged vector equals that peer's record in every compared component, and in an owner-led instance the peer skips precisely the leader's own row, so the fast quorum's two members both hold the committed vector at the same vbal. The residual exposure is therefore one component in a recovery-led phase 1 (leader != owner), where mergeAttributes ignores the leader's own row while the peer may hold a higher value for that row; that needs the peer to know more about the leader's own row than the leader does, which no read path establishes for a live leader (S7-attributes, S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply, S21-quorum-sizes).

handleCommit's NOOP re-proposal branch dereferences leader bookkeeping that message-created records do not have, so a legal NOOP commit for an instance the replica owns terminates the handler; the direct check for claim C4-noop-commit-without-bookkeeping confirmed in scope that a record created by a recovery-led PreAccept plus the commit raises a nil pointer dereference and leaves the instance uncommitted. The run loop has no recover, so the panic is inferred to end the process; the history that leaves a restarted owner in that state and the client-side consequence of the same NOOP recovery remain unread (S13-handleCommit, S9-handlePreAccept, S3-run-dispatch).

handleAcceptReply returns whenever a reply's ballot differs from the round's, so the nack branch behind that gate never runs and a peer that answers with a higher ballot is ignored rather than counted as a rejection; the direct check for claim C7 confirmed nacks 0 and no reaction, and the pre-accept side has no rejection signal either (PreAcceptReply copies the request's ballot and handlePreAccept returns silently for a smaller ballot), so progress after a rejection depends on the 10s execution timeout rather than on the handlers (S12-handleAcceptReply, S11-handleAccept, S4-execute-loop).

with recording enabled, the phase-1 entry records metadata through the recovering replica's own row while installing the instance under the owner's row, so a recovery-led phase 1 either records a different instance's ballot context or terminates on an absent record; the direct check for claim C9-durable-recorder-uses-the-instance-row confirmed the nil dereference with Durable true and an empty own row, and the case where that slot exists is still unread (S8-handlePropose-startPhase1, S19-durable-record).
before.rationale: Both core relationships are traced through real entry points (client propose to phase 1 to pre-accept replies to fast or slow decision to commit install, and ballot promise to nack-driven prepare to recovery sub-cases) and their connection is stated in terms of the per-instance record, the highest-vbal reply rule, the committed short-circuit and the ballot comparison that rejects old replies. The remaining questions are local anomalies inside handlers rather than missing formation, authority-transition or old-work handling, so the overview is recorded as usable with those anomalies kept as open_details and as the first Candidate's discriminator.

the command value codec frames a value's length in a two-byte field on both sides, while the client's command size is configuration-driven; the direct check for claim C10-command-value-length-survives-the-wire confirmed that a 70000-byte value is written as 70013 bytes but decoded as 4464 bytes with only 4477 bytes consumed, so the value is shortened and the rest of the stream is left for the next message. The default configuration's 1000-byte commands never reach the boundary, and what a replica reader does with the shifted stream is unread (S37-state-value-codec, S38-client-command-size).

after.reason: the value and command wire codecs frame every command a replica sends or receives; they carry no protocol decision, but the direct check for claim C10-command-value-length-survives-the-wire confirmed that a value beyond the two-byte length field is silently shortened while its bytes remain in the stream, which the default 1000-byte command size does not reach (S37-state-value-codec, S38-client-command-size).

selections.rationale: Second scenario for the same obligation, covering the consequence the first check left open: the leftover bytes of a truncated value shift the stream, so the next command in the same buffer decodes to garbage. The harness writes a 70000-byte value followed by a small command and decodes both in order; the local construction run shows the second command with op 197, an arbitrary key and a 53198-byte value, with 12341 bytes remaining, so the trust the codec places in the length field destroys the following command as well. The trusted runner and a fresh correspondence review decide the formal outcome.

Semantic review of the second scenario for C10-command-value-length-survives-the-wire (artifact 1f094469…, executed as 8628f4fc…). The item assesses requirement versus predicate, the concatenation premise, the oracle, identity, and the bounded consequences.

F2 scope clarification on the accepted C1 unit, using the C3 claim and its reviewed check as the new basis, so the attribution the superseded artifact blurred is stated in the claim itself. The obligation, its sources, conditions and artifacts are unchanged; only the scope text gains the boundary and names C3.

Re-execution of the C1 check against the current claim version. The F2 scope clarification amended the claim's scope text (naming C3 for the applied-state proposition) without changing the obligation, its sources or its conditions, but the framework requires new execution when a direct check's semantic inputs change, so the three-property plan is submitted again: adoption at the resolution, the recoverer-versus-committed-peer comparison and agreement across replicas after the Commit broadcast. The harness bytes are the reviewed driven version, and the earlier artifacts' observations are unchanged; what is needed is a fresh execution bound to claim version 2 plus a current-version correspondence review.

The observation is a consequence of the requirement rather than the requirement's own premise, and the accepted claim's scope list names exactly that consequence as excluded (execution of the instance and client-visible replies). Entry and observation: the harness applies each record with Exec.executeCommand directly and probes the store with a GET command, which is a declared substitution (the production executeCommands loop, watermark advancement and the recovery timeout are not exercised); the records' COMMITTED status is by construction, and the three values printed in the event are read from the replicated store rather than derived from a context expected to change. Oracle and identity: comparing the three printed values for one instance and one key is a fair encoding of applied-state agreement, and the instance identity is shared with the prerequisite reply, so the failure is not an artefact of correlation. Contrary evidence and the reason for the negative judgment: the element that conflicts is the claim's own excluded list, which the source of record for the accepted obligation states; a consequence outside that scope can still be true and valuable, but confirming it under this claim would treat an independent limit as a confirmation gate, so the artifact should either drop the applied-state property or the proposition should be fixed as its own obligation whose scope includes applying the instance to the state machine. The rest of the artifact (the correction that drives every queued round and re-reads InstanceSpace) reproduces the earlier reviewed findings and does not itself change them.

items.rationale: Requirement versus predicate: the accepted claim is that a slow-quorum reply reporting the instance COMMITTED must be adopted; the plan's observable property asserts adopted_committed on the resolution event, and the harness prints instance_status and command_after in the same event, so the assertion is checkable against the raw fields rather than only through the derived boolean. Entry and caller duties: the recovery is entered directly through startRecoveryForInstance instead of the executeCommands timeout, and the peer's COMMITTED record is prepared rather than produced by a proposal and commit round; both substitutions are declared in the claim's scope and in the harness legality, and neither is needed for the resolution step the claim is about, because the resolution reads only the record, the reply slice and the running ballot. Oracle: adopted_committed is computed by the harness as an OR of two status fields, and the same event carries the status the code actually stored, so a change in the protocol's status semantics would show up in instance_status as well. Identity: the prerequisite and the resolution event share instance 1.0, which is the instance the harness seeds and drives, so correlation is non-trivial and monotone; the identity is written by the harness rather than read from the record, which is noted as a limitation rather than a defect because the harness constructs exactly one instance. Legal history: the prepared COMMITTED record corresponds to a state some history produced, but the trigger path is substituted, so the item is scoped to the resolution decision. Observation path and completion: all handlers are synchronous in the harness, the resolution is observed after handlePrepareReply returns, and the emitted message code is retained, so no wait or join is implied. Counterevidence: the alternative reading (the local record's new ballot legitimately outranks an older committed vbal) is recorded in the claim grounding and is not settled by this check; the item therefore does not promote the finding beyond the reviewed correspondence of predicate and observation. Contrary evidence and alternatives: the two reservations I hold are explained rather than hidden. First, the trigger (executeCommands timeout) and the production of the committed record are substituted, which limits the claim to the resolution decision; second, an alternative reading is that a recovering replica is only required to adopt the value with the highest vbal and that its own newly made ballot legitimately outranks an older committed ballot. I judge the alternative untenable because vbal records the ballot at which a value was accepted, while the recovering replica's fresh ballot carries no accepted value, and because the ignored reply reports COMMITTED, which is the one status the protocol treats as final; the check therefore corresponds to the written obligation, and the reservation is recorded so a later review can challenge it on sources rather than being surprised by it.
items.report_title: 恢复阶段忽略已提交回复
items.report_answer: 构造历史中恢复者把新 ballot 当作自己的 VBallot 上报，使 vbal=0 的 COMMITTED 回复被 element.VBallot >= lb.ballot 的比较跳过：实例最终停留在 PREACCEPTED 并以 NOOP 重新进入阶段 1（adopted_committed=false），而对端仍持有已提交命令。该观察的适用范围限于检查声明的前置条件（直接进入 startRecoveryForInstance、对端已提交记录为预备状态），接受阶段的后续完成与执行后果不在本次检查范围内。

instance identity is a harness literal because the harness drives one instance
the consequence after the resolution (accept-round completion, execution divergence) is outside this check and remains a separate question

items.rationale: Requirement versus predicates: the obligation is that a slow-quorum reply reporting the instance COMMITTED is adopted; the first property asserts adopted_committed on the resolution event, and the second asserts vectors_match on the outcome event, which is the agreement form of the same requirement for the accept path. Both predicates are read from fields the harness prints together with the raw status, command and accept count, and the run reproduced adopted_committed false and vectors_match false with recoverer_command NONE against peer_committed_command PUT and accept_oks 1. Entry, schedule and completion: the harness drives Prepare/PrepareReply, the phase-1 restart's PreAccept/PreAcceptReply and the resulting Accept/AcceptReply in order, re-reading InstanceSpace after every delivery because startPhase1 replaces the record object, so the accept count that moves 0 to 1 and the COMMITTED status are read from the record the handlers actually wrote; the earlier mismatch (accept count read during the phase-1 reply, Accept never delivered) is fixed and the trailing diagnostic shows the Commit the recoverer broadcast. Oracle: vectors_match is the conjunction of the recoverer having committed and its command equalling the peer's, which is exactly the agreement question for one instance; the identity fields correlate the prerequisite reply and the outcome through the instance, not through the compared values. Legality: the peer's COMMITTED record is prepared rather than produced by a proposal round and the trigger is substituted, both declared in the claim scope; the rounds under test are the real handlers. Counterevidence and alternatives: the remaining reservations are that the property passes vacuously when the recoverer does not commit, that the propagation of the recoverer's Commit to other replicas is not driven, and that the alternative reading (a fresh ballot may legitimately outrank an older committed vbal) is answered for this path because the recoverer ends committed with a different command for an instance another replica already committed, which is the disagreement itself.

items.report_answer: 在被驱动的完整恢复路径上，已提交副本报告 COMMITTED(PUT) 时恢复者仍以 NOOP 重启阶段一并完成接受轮（accept_oks 0→1），最终自己提交 COMMITTED(NOOP)：vectors_match=false，即同一实例出现两个不同的已提交命令向量。该观察覆盖本轮驱动的全部轮次与最终记录，超出该路径的后果（其它副本的提交传播、客户端可见性）不在本次检查范围内。
limitations: the outcome property is a conditional: if the recoverer never commits, vectors_match is true and the property would hold vacuously; the outcome event prints recoverer_committed so the applicability is visible
the peer's COMMITTED record is prepared and the recovery is entered directly, so this check fixes the resolution and accept rounds, not the history that produced the commit
the recoverer's Commit propagation to the other replicas and any client-visible effect are not driven
the first property's review for the earlier artifact remains valid; this review covers the corrected artifact and its re-execution

items.rationale: Requirement versus predicates: the obligation is that a slow-quorum reply reporting the instance COMMITTED is adopted; the three properties encode its resolution form (adopted_committed), its two-record agreement form (vectors_match) and now its cluster form (all_committed_match) after the recoverer's Commit broadcast. Each predicate is read together with the raw fields the harness prints (status, per-replica command, accept count), and the retained stream shows replica0 NONE, replica1 PUT, replica2 NONE with all_committed_match false. Entry and schedule: the Commit is produced by the real bcastCommit inside handleAcceptReply, and it is delivered through the real wire form to the already-committed replica, where handleCommit returns early because the status is already COMMITTED, and to the third replica, which installs the command as a legal receiver would; the third replica's absence during the earlier rounds is a harness schedule choice, not a protocol assumption. Oracle: the property compares the committed command of each replica for one instance and identity field, which is the agreement question itself; the comparison is not derived from a context expected to change. Legal history: the already-committed record is a prepared state, so the check fixes the recovery rounds and the propagation, and treats a replica's COMMITTED record as the protocol's own evidence of a chosen value, which is how a PrepareReply with status COMMITTED is treated in the resolution under review. Observation path and completion: every handler is synchronous, the event is emitted after both deliveries, and the trailing diagnostic shows the messages the recoverer emitted, so no wait, join or cleanup duty is implied. Contrary evidence and alternatives: the reservations I hold are recorded as limitations rather than suppressed, namely that the committed records are prepared rather than produced by a proposal round, that the third property is an internal-record statement because the state machines are not executed, and that a reader who rejects the prepared COMMITTED record as evidence of a chosen value would also have to reject the protocol's own use of that status in the resolution.

items.rationale: Requirement versus predicate: the obligation is that each field the recorder writes can be recovered at the offset where the writer placed it, and the predicate asserts bal_field_present on the header event; the retained run shows the header in hex with bal_field_present false, vbal_at_0 true, status_at_4 true and seq_at_5 true, so the derived boolean is checkable against the printed bytes and the printed written values. Entry and caller duty: the recorder runs only when Durable is true, which the harness sets and the prerequisite event reports together with the instance identity and the written field values; sync is called as the production callers do, and no other caller duty is needed for a record of one instance. Oracle: the comparison is against the value the harness asked the recorder to write, with distinct nonzero values so a default-zero buffer cannot pass by accident, and the deps region is left out of the comparison rather than silently assumed. Identity: the write-request prerequisite and the header event share instance 0.0, so the observation is correlated with the write it judges rather than with array order. Constructed input and legality: the claim's applicability is exactly a single recorder call with Durable true and distinct bal, vbal, Status and Seq, so a constructed instance is the full premise here; the alternative reading recorded in the claim (that the layout deliberately stores vbal in place of bal) is what a reviewer would have to accept to reject the finding, and the source shows both a bal write and a buffer sized 9+4N, which that reading would make vestigial. Observation path and completion: the harness writes, syncs, closes and reads the file back before emitting the event, so the observation completes without any wait, join or cleanup duty. Contrary evidence is reflected as limits rather than suppressed: no in-repository reader fixes the intended layout, the shipped run.go passes durable=false, and only one record is observed.

items.rationale: Requirement versus predicate: the accepted claim requires that a reply reporting the instance COMMITTED be adopted; the added property instead asserts that, after each replica applies the instance it holds committed, the state machines agree on the instance's key. The observation is a consequence of the requirement rather than the requirement's own premise, and the accepted claim's scope list names exactly that consequence as excluded (execution of the instance and client-visible replies). Entry and observation: the harness applies each record with Exec.executeCommand directly and probes the store with a GET command, which is a declared substitution (the production executeCommands loop, watermark advancement and the recovery timeout are not exercised); the records' COMMITTED status is by construction, and the three values printed in the event are read from the replicated store rather than derived from a context expected to change. Oracle and identity: comparing the three printed values for one instance and one key is a fair encoding of applied-state agreement, and the instance identity is shared with the prerequisite reply, so the failure is not an artefact of correlation. Contrary evidence and the reason for the negative judgment: the element that conflicts is the claim's own excluded list, which the source of record for the accepted obligation states; a consequence outside that scope can still be true and valuable, but confirming it under this claim would treat an independent limit as a confirmation gate, so the artifact should either drop the applied-state property or the proposition should be fixed as its own obligation whose scope includes applying the instance to the state machine. The rest of the artifact (the correction that drives every queued round and re-reads InstanceSpace) reproduces the earlier reviewed findings and does not itself change them.

the event is reproducible in the retained stream (applied_state_divergence with peer_value 04 and recoverer_value (void)), so the objection is about scope and attribution rather than about the observation (check 2f186bc17e13432fae3b653b42e46941)

the harness invokes Exec.executeCommand directly, so scheduling, watermarks and the recovery timeout are outside even the substituted execution path

items.rationale: Requirement versus predicate: claim C3 requires that replicas holding the same instance committed apply the same effect for the instance's key, and the property asserts applied_match on the applied_state_divergence event; the retained run shows peer_value 04 against recoverer_value and third_value (void) with applied_match false, and the same event prints the command each replica held, so the applied difference is tied to the different committed vectors rather than to an unstated assumption. Entry and caller duties: the harness drives the recovery, the accept round and the Commit broadcast as before, then applies each record with Exec.executeCommand and probes the store with a GET command; the claim's scope now includes applying the instance and excludes the production loop, watermarks, timing and client-visible replies, and the harness substitutions are declared in the plan's semantic changes and uncertainties. Oracle and identity: the three printed values are read from each replica's replicated store for one key, the claim fixes the key as the one the committed commands touch, and the instance identity is shared with the prerequisite reply, so correlation is monotonic and the comparison is not derived from a context expected to change. Legal history: the committed records come from the same driven path as the confirmed C1 checks (recoverer and third replica NOOP, peer PUT), so the input is the observed consequence of the confirmed defect rather than a fabricated state. Contrary evidence and alternatives: the alternative reading that execution lies outside any obligation about adopting a value is exactly why this proposition is its own claim; the reservations that remain are recorded as limitations, namely direct execution instead of the production loop, one instance and one key, and the prepared committed record. The item therefore clears correspondence for C3 rather than extending C1.

one instance and one key are compared; other keys and repeated instances are not
the committed records are prepared/driven as in the C1 checks, so the history that produced them is not constructed

items.rationale: Requirement versus predicates: the three monitored properties encode the accepted C1 obligation and nothing else; the applied-state event is still printed by the harness but no monitor selects it, so the executed checker set matches the accepted scope exactly. Entry, schedule and completion: the harness is the reviewed driven version (Prepare/PrepareReply, the phase-1 restart's PreAccept and reply, the Accept and its reply, the Commit broadcast, with InstanceSpace re-read after every delivery), so the observations come from the records the handlers wrote. Oracle and identity: the same assertions and identity correlation as the reviewed three-property artifact, with the committed_reply prerequisite as admission alias for each monitor. Legal history: the prepared COMMITTED record and direct recovery entry remain declared in the claim scope. Contrary evidence and alternatives: the alternative that the applied-state observation should be confirmable under C1 is answered by claim C3, which owns that proposition and has its own reviewed check; the reservations that remain for this artifact are the ones already recorded (prepared committed record, substituted trigger) and are unchanged.
items.report_title: C1 检查集已仅含范围内属性
items.report_answer: 该工件执行的检查集只含三条范围内属性：解析处的采纳（adopted_committed=false）、恢复者与已提交副本的向量比较（vectors_match=false）、以及提交广播后三副本的一致性（all_committed_match=false）；应用层一致性不再由任何监控器选择，因此它不再进入 C1 的判定。三条属性与已复核的对应关系一致，前置条件、身份字段、法理与驱动轮次均未改变。
limitations: the harness still prints the applied-state event; only the monitor set excludes it, which is the point of this artifact
the prepared COMMITTED record and the direct recovery entry remain substitutions declared in the claim scope

items.rationale: Requirement versus predicate: the claim is that a legal NOOP commit for an instance the replica owns must be processed without dereferencing absent bookkeeping and without terminating the replica; the predicate asserts panicked == false on the commit-result event, and the retained run reports panicked true with the panic value, plus no_effect true, so the assertion is evaluated on printed fields rather than inferred. Entry and message legality: the record is created by the real handlePreAccept for (Replica 0, Instance 0) at ballot 3 with one PUT command, which is what a recovery-led phase 1 sends to the owner, and the commit is a well-formed single NONE command at ballot 4 with matching replica and instance, which is what the recoverer broadcasts after restarting phase 1 with NOOP; both are protocol messages, so the history is legal for a replica that no longer holds the instance in memory. Oracle and the recover() wrapper: the harness wraps only the delivery in recover so a panic is reported as an event instead of killing the test process; the handler itself is unmodified, and the wrapper is what makes the panic observable rather than what creates it, which the printed panic value confirms. Identity: the prerequisite record event and the commit-result event share instance 0.0, so the observation is tied to the record under test. Inference to termination: the run loop dispatches handlers directly in its select statement with no recover, so a panic in handleCommit propagates out of the loop and ends the process; that step is a source-based inference and is recorded as a limitation rather than as an observed process exit, because the harness does not drive the loop. Contrary evidence and alternatives: the alternative reading that such a record can never belong to the owner is contradicted by the message-created record, and the remaining reservations (dispatcher not modelled, single instance, no history) are recorded as limitations. The item therefore clears correspondence for C4 while keeping the inference boundary explicit.
items.report_title: NOOP 提交使实例所有者空指针崩溃
items.report_answer: 由消息创建记录（无 leader bookkeeping）的实例所有者收到一条合法的单 NONE 命令 Commit 后，handleCommit 在重提议分支解引用 inst.lb.clientProposals 触发空指针 panic（事件 panic_value 为 invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference），且该提交未生效（no_effect=true）。运行循环对该处理器没有 recover，因此该 panic 会终止副本进程；这一推断属于限制说明，harness 只观察到 panic 本身。
limitations: the harness observes the panic, not the replica process terminating; the termination step follows from the run loop having no recover and is an inference
the history that would make a recovery-led PreAccept reach a restarted owner is not constructed; the check fixes the two messages and the record state
the client-side consequence of the same NOOP recovery is a separate question and is not part of this check

items.rationale: Requirement versus predicate: the claim is that the owner installs a single-NONE commit and re-proposes the admitted operation rather than dropping it, and the predicate asserts reproposed_on_channel == 1 on the commit event; the retained run prints proposal_admitted with bookkeeping true and pending 1, then noop_commit_at_owner with instance_status COMMITTED, pending_after 0 and reproposed_on_channel 1, so the assertion is evaluated on the printed fields. Entry and message legality: the harness admits the operation with the real handlePropose (which attaches the GPropose to the instance bookkeeping and broadcasts the PreAccept) and delivers the commit that a recoverer broadcasts after restarting phase 1 with NOOP for the owner's instance; both are protocol messages and the owner-alive record state is the ordinary one for an admitted operation. Oracle: the three printed quantities together distinguish re-proposal from dropping (pending cleared and one proposal waiting on the channel), and the count is the channel length rather than a derived boolean. Identity: the prerequisite admission event and the commit event share instance 0.0. Observation path and completion: both handlers are synchronous and their effects on the bookkeeping and channel are read immediately after the call, so no wait or cleanup duty is implied. Contrary evidence and alternatives: the claim's scope deliberately excludes the restarted-owner case, where the same handler instead dereferences absent bookkeeping and terminates the replica, which is confirmed separately as claim C4; the remaining reservations are recorded as limitations, namely that the re-proposed operation's later commit and execution are not driven and that the run loop's own handling of the channel is not modelled.
items.report_title: 所有者存活时 NOOP 提交会重新提议已接纳操作
items.report_answer: 在所有者仍持有该操作的情况下，handlePropose 接纳操作后（bookkeeping=true，pending=1），一条合法的单 NONE Commit 使实例进入 COMMITTED，pending 清零且提案被重新放回提议通道（reproposed_on_channel=1），即操作未被丢弃而是重新进入决策流程；该结论仅覆盖所有者存活情形，重启后无 bookkeeping 的情形属于 C4 的崩溃结论。
limitations: only the owner-alive case is covered; the restarted-owner case is claim C4's confirmed crash for the same handler
the re-proposed operation's later commit, execution and client reply are not driven, so the client's completion is not observed here
the commit is delivered directly to the handler rather than through the run loop

items.rationale: Requirement versus predicate: claim C6 asserts that a replica the deployment promoted to leader must adopt a reply reporting the instance COMMITTED, and the three properties assert adoption at the resolution, the recoverer-versus-peer comparison and agreement after the Commit broadcast; the retained stream shows the seed with is_leader true, max_recv_ballot 5 and the self VBallot 6, then adopted_committed false together with the derived comparisons, so the predicates are evaluated on printed fields. Entry and variant legality: the master designates a leader in the shipped configuration and calls Replica.BeTheLeader on it, which sets IsLeader; makeBallot then raises the new ballot past maxRecvBallot, and startRecoveryForInstance reports that raised ballot as the replica's own VBallot, so the variant differs from the reviewed non-promoted case only in the ballot value while the comparison that skips older-vbal replies is unchanged. Oracle and identity: the same assertions, prerequisite and instance identity correlation as the non-promoted artifact. Observation path and completion: the harness drives the queued rounds and re-reads InstanceSpace after each delivery, as in the reviewed version. Contrary evidence and alternatives: the reservation that the deployment flag might change the outcome is answered by this run, and the remaining reservations are recorded as limitations, namely that a real ballot history is modelled as one maxRecvBallot value, that the master's promotion is a sourced premise rather than an executed step, and that the committed record is prepared. C1's confirmed scope (IsLeader false) is untouched and this claim covers only the promoted variant.
items.report_title: 被提升为 leader 的副本同样忽略已提交回复
items.report_answer: 在提升变体下（IsLeader=true、maxRecvBallot=5），恢复者的新 ballot 为 6 并作为自身 VBallot 上报，对端 vbal=0 的 COMMITTED 回复被跳过（adopted_committed=false），接受轮完成（accept_oks 0→1），恢复者以 NOOP 提交而对端保持 PUT（vectors_match=false、all_committed_match=false），应用状态同样分叉。该结论属于 C6（仅限提升变体），C1 的已确认范围保持不变。
limitations: a real promoted replica's ballot history is modelled as a single maxRecvBallot value; the run exercises the raising loop's effect, not a long history
the master's promotion is grounded in the master and configuration sources but is not executed in the harness
the peer's committed record is prepared and the recovery is entered directly, as in the non-promoted check

items.rationale: Requirement versus predicate: the claim is that a reply whose ballot exceeds the accept round's ballot must be recorded as a rejection so the leader can make a new ballot and prepare again, and the predicate asserts nacks == 1 on the reply event; the retained run prints reply_ballot 5 against the round's last_tried_ballot 3 with nacks 0, accept_oks 0, prepare_sent false and the status unchanged, so the assertion is evaluated on the handler's own counters. Entry and legality: the round is built with the package's own instance and bookkeeping constructors in the state a leader reaches after the accept branch (lb.status ACCEPTED with the round's ballot), and the reply is the value handleAccept sends when its stored bal exceeds the accept ballot, so both sides are implementation-produced states rather than invented inputs. Oracle and identity: the counters read after the call are the handler's own bookkeeping values, and the round and reply events share instance 1.0. Observation path and completion: the handler is synchronous, its effect is read immediately, and the check asks nothing about later rounds, so no wait or cleanup duty is implied. Contrary evidence and bounded consequence: the pre-accept side cannot produce a differing reply at all because PreAcceptReply copies the request's ballot and handlePreAccept returns silently when the request's ballot is too small, so this handler holds the only rejection branch — and the 10s execution timeout can still drive the instance into recovery, which is why the claim is scoped as a delay on the collision path rather than a stall. The limitations record that the timeout path is not exercised and that only one reply is delivered, so the majority-nack consequence of the branch is outside this check.
items.report_title: 接受轮的高 ballot 回复未被记为拒绝
items.report_answer: leader 处于 ACCEPTED 轮（lastTriedBallot=3）时收到 ballot=5 的 AcceptReply，处理结果 nacks=0、accept_oks=0、未发出任何消息、状态不变：ballot 相等性判断先返回，使得其后的 nack 分支永远不会执行，副本因此不会因为被拒绝而重新 prepare。该结论的后果限于碰撞路径上的延迟，因为 10s 执行超时仍可驱动恢复。
limitations: the timeout-driven recovery that can also advance the instance is not exercised, so the consequence is bounded to a delay
only one reply is delivered, so the branch's majority-nack consequence is not reached
the round is constructed rather than driven through the accept branch of handlePreAcceptReply

items.rationale: Requirement versus predicate: the claim is that a blocked instance must be enqueued for recovery once the executor's grace period elapses, and the predicate asserts enqueued == true on the recovery event; the retained run reports true, with the enqueued replica and instance fields (1 and 0) independently corroborating which operation was admitted. Entry and schedule: the blocked record is built with the package's own constructor in the state a replica reaches when it has an instance number but no committed commands for it, the executor goroutine is the implementation's own loop started directly instead of by New(), and the harness reads instancesToRecover rather than letting the run loop consume it; the prerequisite prints the record's status, command presence, crtInstance and ExecedUpTo, so an unreached premise would be visible. Oracle and identity: the comparison is against whether the channel received the instance, and the identity is shared with the prerequisite. Observation path and completion: the select has a bounded alternative that prints enqueued false, so a non-observation is recorded rather than hidden, and the goroutine is stopped by the harness's deferred Shutdown flag. Contrary evidence and limits: the wall-clock grace period follows the loop's per-iteration counter rather than a clock, so the measured wait is a diagnostic; only the enqueue is observed, not the recovery it triggers; and one blocked row is exercised. No counterevidence was found that the duty fails in this scope.
items.report_title: 执行器超时会将被阻塞实例入队恢复
items.report_answer: 行 1 被一条无命令且未提交的记录阻塞时（前置事件：status 0、has_commands false、crtInstance 0、ExecedUpTo -1），执行器在约 12.6 秒后把该实例入队：enqueued true、enqueued_replica 1、enqueued_instance 0。即被拒绝的接受轮所依赖的时间驱动恢复路径确实存在，代价是一次约 12.6 秒的等待（该值随后台循环计数方式而定，属诊断而非规格）。
limitations: the measured wait (~12.6s) follows the loop's one-millisecond-per-iteration counter, so it is a diagnostic rather than a specified deadline
the check observes the enqueue, not the recovery that consumes it, and only one blocked row is exercised
the executor goroutine is started by the harness rather than by epaxos.New, so the run loop's role is outside the check

items.rationale: Requirement versus predicate: the claim is that the recorder receives the record of the instance being written and must not dereference a record the replica does not hold, and the predicate asserts panicked == false; the retained run reports panicked true with the nil-pointer panic value while the owner's row does hold the new record, so the assertion is evaluated on printed fields and the failure is localised to the recording call. Entry and legality: the call is the one the prepare resolution makes when it restarts phase 1 with a recovered command (sub-cases 5 and 6), the empty own row is the state of a replica that has not held that instance (a restarted replica), and the recording is enabled through the constructor's durable flag, so no protocol code was altered and the instance setup is the implementation's own. Oracle and identity: panicked and the two row flags are read after the call, and the prerequisite and result events share instance 1.0. Contrary evidence and bounded consequences: the shipped run.go passes durable=false, so this path is inert in the default deployment; the check exercises the nil case only, leaving the case where the recovering replica's own row happens to hold an instance at that number — where the source implies another instance's metadata would be recorded — as an explicit unknown rather than a claim; and the panic is observed by the harness, with the process-death step following from the run loop having no recover as in the earlier crash review. This claim is kept separate from C2, which concerns the layout of the record the recorder writes: here the complaint is which instance's record is recorded at all.
items.report_title: 恢复主导的阶段一按自身行记录元数据
items.report_answer: 在 Durable=true 且恢复者自身行没有该实例的情况下，startPhase1 为他人实例写入记录：实例已安装在所有者行（owner_record_written=true），但元数据记录调用解引用恢复者自身行的实例（own_row_record_written=false）并以空指针 panic 结束（panicked=true）。因此记录的坐标与实际写入的实例不一致；该结论的后果限于启用 Durable 的调用方（默认配置为 false），槽位恰好存在时的错误记录仍是未验证的隐含问题。
limitations: the case where the recovering replica's own row holds an instance at that number is not exercised; the source implies it would record another instance's metadata
the shipped configuration passes durable=false, so the consequence is bounded to callers that enable recording
the harness observes the panic rather than the replica process terminating

items.rationale: Requirement versus predicate: the claim is that the metadata recorded for a phase-1 write must belong to the instance being written, and the predicate asserts recorded_matches_new_instance == true; the retained run reports false with recorded_matches_own_row true, so the assertion is evaluated on the decoded values and the comparison points at the other instance. Entry and legality: the call is the phase-1 entry with the owner's coordinates, which is what the prepare resolution invokes when it restarts phase 1 for another replica's instance, and two rows holding an instance at the same number is the ordinary shape of per-replica rows rather than an invented state. Oracle and observation: the harness decodes the bytes with the layout the recorder itself writes (status at byte 4, seq at bytes 5 to 8) and compares the decoded seq against both candidate records, which is what makes the attribution possible; claim C2 shows that layout is not readable as its writes suggest, and that caveat is recorded as a limitation rather than hidden, since the comparison here only needs to identify which record's values were written. Identity: the prerequisite and result events share instance 1.0. Contrary evidence and limits: the shipped configuration passes durable=false, so the path is inert by default; only one instance number is exercised; and the check does not decode the deps region. No counterevidence was found that the duty holds in this scope.
items.report_title: 自身行已占用时记录了他实例的元数据
items.report_answer: 当恢复者自身行在同一编号已存在另一实例（own_row_seq 858993459、ACCEPTED）时，阶段一为所有者实例写记录：写入的 seq 等于自身行的 seq 而非新实例的 seq 0（recorded_matches_new_instance=false、recorded_matches_own_row=true，状态为自身行的 ACCEPTED），即稳定存储收到的是另一实例的 ballot 上下文，且不会 panic。该结论限于启用记录的调用方（默认 durable=false），解码使用记录器自身布局这一限制也已注明。
limitations: the recorded bytes are decoded with the recorder's own write layout, which claim C2 shows is not the layout its field writes imply
the durable path is inert in the shipped configuration (durable=false)
one instance number and one occupied own row are exercised; the deps region is not decoded

items.rationale: Requirement versus predicate: the claim is that a value the client can build must survive the codec or be rejected, and the predicate asserts value_matches on the round-trip event; the retained run reports false with the declared length, the decoded length and the consumed bytes all printed, so the assertion is evaluated on the codec's own output rather than on an inferred quantity. Entry and legality: both directions of the codec are the implementation's own and the harness calls them directly; the premise that such a value can enter the protocol rests on the command size being a configuration parameter (aws.conf sets 1000; the field carries up to 65535) rather than on a client drive, which is recorded as a limitation rather than assumed silently. Oracle and observation: value_matches compares the decoded bytes with the payload the harness built, and the wire-length event shows the encoder emitted all bytes, so the shortening is attributable to the length field rather than to a truncated write; identity is the shared subject field between the prerequisite and the result. Contrary evidence and limits: the shipped configuration's 1000-byte commands never reach the boundary, no replica reader is exercised so the desynchronisation's consequence on the following message is not observed, and whether the client library caps the size it builds was not read. No counterevidence was found that the codec preserves values in this scope.
items.report_title: 命令值长度在网络上被静默截断
items.report_answer: 经真实编解码往返：声明 70000 字节的值在线上写出 70013 字节，解码仅得 4464 字节（70000 mod 65536），且只消费 4477 字节，value_matches=false；剩余字节留在流中会错位后续消息边界。该结论成立的前提是“调用方可以构造超过 65535 字节的值”，这一点由命令大小是配置项支持（默认配置为 1000 字节，未触及该边界）。
limitations: the value is constructed by the harness; the client's own allocation cap was not read, so the premise that a caller can reach this size rests on the configuration being a parameter
the shipped configuration uses 1000-byte commands, so the default deployment never reaches the truncation
no replica reader consumes the shifted stream, so the desync's effect on the following message is unobserved

items.rationale: Requirement versus predicate: the claim is that a value the client can build must survive the codec, and this scenario asserts that the command following such a value still decodes to what was written; the retained run reports second_matches false with the decoded op, key and value length printed, so the assertion is evaluated on the decoder's own output. Entry and legality: two Command marshallings in one buffer is how the durable recorder appends commands (each command written in sequence with no per-command framing), which is exactly the consecutive-decode shape the scenario needs; a message carrying an array of commands would be corrupted in the same way because the decoder trusts the value length, which is recorded as a limitation rather than claimed as the exercised input. Oracle and identity: second_matches compares the decoded fields with the command the harness wrote, and the stream identity correlates the prerequisite with the result, so the garbage values are attributable to the shift rather than to correlation. Contrary evidence and limits: the shipped configuration's 1000-byte commands never reach the boundary; no replica reader consumes the shifted stream, so the reader's own reaction (an unknown message type once the framing is lost) is unobserved; and the harness does not exercise a message's array framing. No counterevidence was found that the following command survives in this scope.
items.report_title: 超长值之后的命令解码为垃圾数据
items.report_answer: 同一缓冲中先写 70000 字节值的命令、再写一条小命令，解码第一条只取回 4464 字节后，第二条被解码为 op 197、任意键与 53198 字节值（second_matches=false，剩余 12341 字节）：被截断的值不仅自身缩短，还破坏了其后的命令边界。该结论适用于记录器那种无框架的命令级联（recordCommands 逐条 Marshal），默认 1000 字节命令不会触达该边界。
limitations: the input models the durable recorder's unframed command sequence rather than a message's array framing, which would be corrupted the same way but was not exercised
the shipped configuration's 1000-byte commands never reach the boundary
no replica reader consumes the shifted stream, so the reader-side reaction is unobserved

Confirmed violation of: When Durable is enabled, recordInstanceMetadata writes the current bal, vbal, Status, Seq and Deps of an instance into the stable store; the record it produces must let each field it writes be recovered at the offset where the writer placed it, so that no value it wrote is silently replaced by another field of the same record.

Measured violation awaiting attribution: Direct-check semantic inputs changed; execution requires rechecking; Direct oracle correspondence remains disputed: Requirement versus predicate: the accepted claim requires that a reply reporting the instance COMMITTED be adopted; the added property instead asserts that, after each replica applies the instance it holds committed, the state machines agree on the instance's key. The observation is a consequence of the requirement rather than the requirement's own premise, and the accepted claim's scope list names exactly that consequence as excluded (execution of the instance and client-visible replies). Entry and observation: the harness applies each record with Exec.executeCommand directly and probes the store with a GET command, which is a declared substitution (the production executeCommands loop, watermark advancement and the recovery timeout are not exercised); the records' COMMITTED status is by construction, and the three values printed in the event are read from the replicated store rather than derived from a context expected to change. Oracle and identity: comparing the three printed values for one instance and one key is a fair encoding of applied-state agreement, and the instance identity is shared with the prerequisite reply, so the failure is not an artefact of correlation. Contrary evidence and the reason for the negative judgment: the element that conflicts is the claim's own excluded list, which the source of record for the accepted obligation states; a consequence outside that scope can still be true and valuable, but confirming it under this claim would treat an independent limit as a confirmation gate, so the artifact should either drop the applied-state property or the proposition should be fixed as its own obligation whose scope includes applying the instance to the state machine. The rest of the artifact (the correction that drives every queued round and re-reads InstanceSpace) reproduces the earlier reviewed findings and does not itself change them.; Open review issue ef6b54abce294555b31a3c9a6ca606ac [S20-exec,S23-state-conflict-apply,S13-handleCommit,S15-handlePrepareReply,S14-recovery-start-prepare]: the accepted claim C1-recovery-adopts-committed-vector lists execution of the instance and client-visible replies under scope.excluded, so the applied-state property tests outside the accepted proposition (claim C1 scope, S20-exec); the event is reproducible in the retained stream (applied_state_divergence with peer_value 04 and recoverer_value (void)), so the objection is about scope and attribution rather than about the observation (check 2f186bc17e13432fae3b653b42e46941)

audit_question.question: When recovery runs for instance (Replica, Instance) and a slow-quorum PrepareReply reports that instance COMMITTED with a command vector, does the recovering replica adopt that committed vector, or does it continue from its own record and restart phase 1 with a different command (NOOP when its record has no commands)?
audit_question.importance: If the committed vector is not adopted, the replicas that already committed and possibly executed the instance keep it while the recovering replica re-proposes another command, so the instance has two competing values: an installed commit that ignores later Commits versus a re-proposal that can be accepted by replicas that do not hold the commit. That is an agreement and state-convergence concern for a crash-recovered replica.
contexts: N=3 with Thrifty
recovering replica holding a default NONE record
peer holding COMMITTED with a command
recovery entered directly through startRecoveryForInstance
event_paths: startRecoveryForInstance seeds the local record and reports the new ballot as its own VBallot
the peer's PrepareReply reports Status COMMITTED at an older vbal
handlePrepareReply resolves and either adopts the committed vector or restarts phase 1

audit_question.question: When Durable is enabled, recordInstanceMetadata writes the current bal, vbal, Status, Seq and Deps of an instance into the stable store. Does the record it produces preserve the value written for bal at the offset where the recorder wrote it, or does a later write of the same record replace it, and does Status land inside the bytes a reader would use for vbal?
audit_question.importance: A record that cannot carry the fields the writer intended hides the ballot context of an instance from any reader of that layout (a recovery path or an external tool), so a replica that restarts from such a record would be missing the value it needs to compare ballots. The consequence is bounded here because the shipped configuration passes durable=false and no reader exists in the snapshot, which is why this is recorded as an implementation-semantics defect rather than a live availability or agreement failure.
contexts: Durable true reached through the constructor argument
one instance with distinct bal, vbal, Status, Seq
event_paths: recordInstanceMetadata builds a 9+4N byte buffer and writes bal, vbal, Status, Seq, Deps
the harness reads back the first 9+4N bytes and reports which written value appears at offset 0

supporting_behavior_ids.B9-recovery-trigger: the ballut context a restarted replica would need comes from the recovery path that consumes such a record

counterevidence: scoped to the source: the function writes bal at [0:4) and then writes vbal at the same bytes before Status at [4) and Seq at [5:9), so the collision is visible in the source itself (S19-durable-record)
scoped to the launched configuration: run.go passes durable=false, so the recorder is inert in the default deployment and no in-repository reader parses the layout (S24-runReplica-epaxos)
unknowns: whether any external tool parses the stable store and expects a particular layout
whether a recovery path from the stable store is intended for a later revision
audit_question.trigger_rationale: This is an A2-supporting question: the persisted bal and vbal are the instance's authority context, the values a restarted replica would need to compare ballots, and the backing behavior is the recorder that writes them. Source reading shows the collision directly (bal and vbal share [0:4), Status occupies [4)), so the check fixes the obligation and observes the produced bytes with the real recorder.

audit_question.question: When one instance is held committed at three replicas with different committed commands for it, does applying each record through the executor leave the same effect for the instance's key, or do the replicas' state machines end up holding different effects for the same instance?
audit_question.importance: Execution is where a committed decision becomes observable state, so an instance that is committed with different commands at different replicas produces different effects for the same key: replicas then serve different values and can never reconcile without rewriting applied state. This is the applied form of the agreement concern and is stated as its own obligation because the adopted-vector claim excludes execution.
contexts: one instance committed at three replicas

selections.rationale: First substantive product of this run: a partial but usable map of the EPaxos replica responsibility (core_overview for both core relationships, seven activities, sixteen behaviors, seven facts, ten surfaced unread boundaries) plus the first Candidate. The Candidate selects the one sourced discrepancy that would matter most if reachable: handlePreAccept stores a received command into InstanceSpace[PreAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler addresses the instance (PreAccept.Replica, Instance) named by the message.

after.purpose: Form a per-instance decision: fix the command, its sequence number and its dependency vector, and advance the instance from tentative pre-accept through accept to commit.
after.realization_summary: handlePropose allocates (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq,deps) from the local conflict tables, records the instance as PREACCEPTED and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers (Thrifty). handlePreAccept recomputes attributes on the receiver and replies with (bal,vbal,seq,deps,CommittedUpTo,status). handlePreAcceptReply merges replies and commits on the fast path when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and allEqual and (for N>7) allCommitted and the ballot is the initial ballot; otherwise the instance moves to ACCEPTED and a majority accept round runs in handleAcceptReply (acceptOKs+1 > N/2), followed by bcastCommit.

after.purpose: Carry the per-instance authority context: which ballot the record is promised to, at which ballot its attributes were last fixed, and which replica may currently advance it.
after.realization_summary: Each Instance keeps bal (highest ballot promised) and vbal (ballot at which the current attributes were established). maxRecvBallot is raised by every received message type and constrains makeBallot, which picks id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and further raised while IsLeader. Ballot comparison gates every message and reply: lower ballots are dropped or nacked, and a majority of nacks lets a replica raise the ballot and run prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead it does.

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

open_details: handlePreAccept's status >= ACCEPTED branch stores the incoming command in InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler uses preAccept.Replica (S9-handlePreAccept); which histories reach that branch is unresolved.

handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal but never records an ACCEPTED status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE; the >= ACCEPTED guards in handlePreAccept and findPreAcceptConflicts therefore only ever see COMMITTED on non-leaders (S11-handleAccept, S9-handlePreAccept, S17-find-conflicts).

handlePrepareReply documents six sub-cases but the guards for sub-cases 3 and 4 are textually identical, so the TryPreAccept-based sub-case appears unreachable (S15-handlePrepareReply, S16-handleTryPreAccept).
handleTryPreAcceptReply's defer-cycle guard counts lb.possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId] inside a loop over q, so the count can only be 0 or N and never equals N/2 (S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply).

recordInstanceMetadata writes bal and vbal into the same [0:4] byte range and stores Status at offset 4 inside a 9+4N header, and no reader of that format exists in the snapshot; the launcher always passes durable = false (S19-durable-record, S24-runReplica-epaxos).
the transconf branch inside Exec.strongconnect computes state.Conflict but performs no action, and run.go passes transconf = false (S20-exec, S24-runReplica-epaxos).
the N<=3 with Thrifty configuration skips the fast-path attribute-equality check while still committing at preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 = 1 (S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S21-quorum-sizes).
after.rationale: Both core relationships are traced through real entry points (client propose to phase 1 to pre-accept replies to fast or slow decision to commit install, and ballot promise to nack-driven prepare to recovery sub-cases) and their connection is stated in terms of the per-instance record, the highest-vbal reply rule, the committed short-circuit and the ballot comparison that rejects old replies. The remaining questions are local anomalies inside handlers rather than missing formation, authority-transition or old-work handling, so the overview is recorded as usable with those anomalies kept as open_details and as the first Candidate's discriminator.

selections.rationale: Source review resolved the Candidate's discriminator without needing execution. The wrong-slot write at epaxos/epaxos.go:809 assigns the received command to InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance], but every other access in handlePreAccept addresses the instance named by the message, (preAccept.Replica, preAccept.Instance). The premise that branch needs -- a local record with Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil -- is not produced by any status-advancing path in the snapshot: handleAccept stores bal, vbal, Seq and Deps but leaves Status at NONE; the leader-side accept and commit transitions (handlePreAcceptReply, handleTryPreAcceptReply, handleAcceptReply) copy lb.cmds and set the command in the same step as the status; handleCommit copies commit.Command, which arrives through the wire format where a nil slice is unmarshalled as a non-nil empty slice; and the only records with nil Cmds are freshly created defaults with Status NONE. The branch is therefore dead code while acceptors do not record acceptance, which is why the wrong-slot write is not reachable today. The map is updated in the same product: Behaviors B3 and B5 record the sourced protection and the answered unknown, and core_overview's first open detail is replaced by the sourced conditional relationship. The remaining, now separated, premise -- whether the accept phase is required to record ACCEPTED on an acceptor, which three guards and one recovery sub-case presuppose -- is carried in feedback for a later question.

feedback.answered: The Candidate's discriminator is resolved on sources: no legal history in the captured snapshot establishes the branch premise. A replica that receives PreAccept can hold Status >= ACCEPTED with Cmds == nil only if some local transition sets ACCEPTED, COMMITTED or EXECUTED without also installing commands. handleAccept stores bal, vbal, Seq and Deps but never writes Status, so an acceptor that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE even though it holds accepted attributes (S11-handleAccept). Every transition that does set Status >= ACCEPTED also sets Cmds in the same handler: handlePreAccept stores the received command when it sets PREACCEPTED/PREACCEPTED_EQ (S9-handlePreAccept), the leader-side accept and commit paths set inst.Cmds from lb.cmds (S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S12-handleAcceptReply, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply), and handleCommit copies commit.Command (S13-handleCommit). A commit command cannot arrive as nil through the wire format: Marshal writes a zero-length prefix and Unmarshal allocates a non-nil empty slice. The only nil-Cmds records are fresh default records with Status NONE (S11-handleAccept, S13-handleCommit, S14-recovery-start-prepare). The line 809 branch is therefore dead code while acceptors do not record acceptance, and the wrong-slot write cannot be reached; the two sourced discrepancies (the LeaderId index and the omitted ACCEPTED status) currently compensate instead of composing into a defect.
remaining: whether the accept phase is required to record ACCEPTED on an acceptor, so that handlePreAccept's >= ACCEPTED guard (S9-handlePreAccept), findPreAcceptConflicts' already-ACCEPTED shortcut (S17-find-conflicts) and handlePrepareReply's sub-case 2 (S15-handlePrepareReply) can observe accept-phase state on a replica that never led the instance
whether the intended acceptor status semantics are external to this snapshot (the corrected EPaxos specification or reference implementation) rather than inferable from in-repository callers
feedback.rationale: The branch premise was the Candidate's open question; enumerating every writer of Instance.Cmds and Instance.Status in the snapshot answers it without execution, so the proposition is explained by the existing (if accidental) protection rather than confirmed as a violated obligation. The consequence chain that would follow if the branch were reachable (wrong-slot command attribution, addressed row left without commands, execution requiring Cmds != nil) stays recorded in the question, but it is not an observed behavior. The separately grounded accept-status premise is a different responsibility and is retained for its own question instead of being folded into this one.

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.
