selections.rationale: Sourced correction and frontier cleanup while the N<=3 fast-path Candidate stays active. Reading handlePreAcceptReply again showed that the committed vector is not the leader's own proposal vector: the merged (seq,deps) produced by mergeAttributes are written back into the leader bookkeeping (lb.deps/lb.seq = merged while lb.status <= PREACCEPTED_EQ) before the branch is chosen, and both the fast-commit branch and the accept branch then install that merged vector. The N<=3 Thrifty exemption therefore does not change which vector is published; what it removes is the requirement that every counted reply already equals that merged vector, which is the step that otherwise either certifies agreement or triggers the accept round that puts the merged vector on a majority. The Candidate's premise is corrected accordingly, and the exposure is now stated precisely: the leader's own record keeps the proposal ballot as vbal while a pre-accepting peer records the same pre-accept ballot, so a recovery selecting by vbal cannot prefer the committed vector over a strictly smaller one held by a peer. In the same product, the two recovery open details are resolved as unreachable dead code in the map (sub-case 4 never runs, taking with it bcastTryPreAccept, handleTryPreAccept, findPreAcceptConflicts, handleTryPreAcceptReply, the possibleQuorum bookkeeping and the deferMap check), and B4 now records the merge-installation guard.

feedback.answered: Two sourced results. First, a correction of the active Candidate's premise: the fast path publishes the merged vector, not the leader's own proposal vector, because handlePreAcceptReply installs lb.deps and lb.seq from mergeAttributes before choosing the branch (lb.deps/lb.seq = merged while lb.status <= PREACCEPTED_EQ) and both the fast-commit branch and the accept branch then copy those merged values into the instance (S10-handlePreAcceptReply). allEqual is therefore not the check that decides which value is committed but the check that certifies every counted reply already holds that merged value; with the N<=3 Thrifty exemption the leader may publish a merged vector that no other replica holds at that ballot (the merged vector strictly dominates each reply's vector whenever a reply contributes a dependency the leader's own vector lacks). formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

open_details: handlePreAccept's status >= ACCEPTED branch stores the incoming command in InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler uses preAccept.Replica (S9-handlePreAccept). Source review of every status-advancing path found no state with Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil: acceptors keep Status NONE, the leader-side accept/commit paths copy commands, and the only nil-Cmds records are fresh defaults with Status NONE. The wrong-slot write is therefore unreachable while acceptors do not record acceptance; the unprotected premise is whether handleAccept is required to record ACCEPTED (S11-handleAccept, S12-handleAcceptReply, S13-handleCommit).

selections.rationale: Feedback-only product that narrows the active Candidate's exposure using source structure, without changing any map object. Comparing how the leader's and the peer's dependency vectors are computed shows why the N<=3 Thrifty equality exemption is sound in the owner-led case and why the recovery-led case is the one that can split: a peer recomputes with updateAttributes starting from the leader's transmitted deps vector and only increases components, and it skips the instance owner's row, so with a single fast-quorum peer the merged vector (componentwise maximum) equals that peer's vector whenever the leader is also the owner, and the leader installs that same merged vector on commit. When the leader is not the owner (recovery sub-case 5/6 restarts phase 1 for another replica's instance), the leader and the peer each skip the owner's row but add their own knowledge to their own rows, so the leader can contribute a component on the leader's row that the peer lacks while the peer contributes one on a different row: the merged vector is then strictly greater than both records and is held only by the leader after its fast commit.

feedback.answered: The exemption's reachable window is now located on sources. updateAttributes only raises the dependency components it is given: it starts from the received deps vector, skips the row of the instance owner named in the message, and for every other row raises deps[q] to the highest conflicting instance known locally (S7-attributes). A pre-accepting peer therefore returns a vector that dominates the leader's transmitted vector componentwise; with one peer (N=3, Thrifty, FastQuorumSize-1 = 1) the leader's merge equals that peer's vector, and the fast-commit branch installs the merged vector into the leader's own record (S10-handlePreAcceptReply). In that owner-led case the committed vector is held at the same vbal by both members of the fast quorum, so a recovery quorum (SlowQuorumSize = 2) must intersect one of them and sees the committed vector. The exemption is therefore not automatically unsafe. The case that can split is a phase 1 restarted for an instance whose owner is another replica (handlePrepareReply sub-case 5 or 6 calls startPhase1 with PreAccept.Replica = owner and LeaderId = recovering replica, S15-handlePrepareReply, S8-handlePropose-startPhase1). There the leader and the peer both skip the owner's row but raise their own rows from their own conflict tables, so the leader can contribute a component on its own row that the peer does not have while the peer contributes another: the merged vector is then strictly greater than either record and is held only by the committing leader, while the peer keeps its smaller vector at the same ballot (S9-handlePreAccept, S10-handlePreAcceptReply).
remaining: whether a recovery whose slow quorum contains the differing peer rather than the committed leader re-proposes the peer's smaller vector for the instance (the highest-vbal selection cannot separate them because both records carry the pre-accept ballot as vbal) (S15-handlePrepareReply)

whether the already-committed leader then refuses the later Commit and keeps the larger vector, freezing two committed vectors for one instance (handleCommit returns early for Status >= COMMITTED) (S13-handleCommit)
whether the two vectors order conflicting instances differently, since the difference is a dependency component on a row whose conflicting command may not yet be committed at the peer (S20-exec)

whether the recovery-led fast commit is reachable with a single peer reply inside the exempted configuration, that is whether an N=3 deployment with a non-owner recovery is a supported history (S24-runReplica-epaxos, S21-quorum-sizes)

The owner-led case is now explained (a single peer's vector dominates and is adopted by both), which is consistent with the source comment that equality need not be checked there. The recovery-led case remains open and is the discriminator a controlled schedule would settle; recording it here keeps the map stable and leaves the Candidate's proposition intact while making the next construction step concrete. formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

open_details: handlePreAccept's status >= ACCEPTED branch stores the incoming command in InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler uses preAccept.Replica (S9-handlePreAccept). Source review of every status-advancing path found no state with Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil: acceptors keep Status NONE, the leader-side accept/commit paths copy commands, and the only nil-Cmds records are fresh defaults with Status NONE. The wrong-slot write is therefore unreachable while acceptors do not record acceptance; the unprotected premise is whether handleAccept is required to record ACCEPTED (S11-handleAccept, S12-handleAcceptReply, S13-handleCommit).

handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal but never records an ACCEPTED status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE; the >= ACCEPTED guards in handlePreAccept and findPreAcceptConflicts therefore only ever see COMMITTED on non-leaders (S11-handleAccept, S9-handlePreAccept, S17-find-conflicts).

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

the N<=3 with Thrifty configuration skips the fast-path attribute-equality check while still committing at preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 = 1. The committed vector is the merge of the leader's own and the counted replies' (seq,deps) (mergeAttributes, installed into the bookkeeping before the branch choice), so the exemption does not publish the leader's own proposal vector; what it removes is the requirement that every counted reply already equal that merged vector, which is the step that otherwise either forces agreement or triggers the accept round that puts the merged vector on a majority. With exactly one counted peer the merged vector equals that peer's record in every compared component, and in an owner-led instance the peer skips precisely the leader's own row, so the fast quorum's two members both hold the committed vector at the same vbal. The residual exposure is therefore one component in a recovery-led phase 1 (leader != owner), where mergeAttributes ignores the leader's own row while the peer may hold a higher value for that row; that needs the peer to know more about the leader's own row than the leader does, which no read path establishes for a live leader (S7-attributes, S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply, S21-quorum-sizes).

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known. In the captured implementation the recovering replica also raises its own record's vbal to the newly made ballot before it builds its PrepareReply, so the resolution's running maximum starts above any value that other replicas accepted at older vbals; the direct checks for claim C1-recovery-adopts-committed-vector confirmed in scope that this lets a recovery commit a NOOP vector for an instance another replica already holds as COMMITTED with a real command, and that the recoverer's Commit broadcast does not repair the disagreement.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

open_details: handlePreAccept's status >= ACCEPTED branch stores the incoming command in InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler uses preAccept.Replica (S9-handlePreAccept). Source review of every status-advancing path found no state with Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil: acceptors keep Status NONE, the leader-side accept/commit paths copy commands, and the only nil-Cmds records are fresh defaults with Status NONE. The wrong-slot write is therefore unreachable while acceptors do not record acceptance; the unprotected premise is whether handleAccept is required to record ACCEPTED (S11-handleAccept, S12-handleAcceptReply, S13-handleCommit).

handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal but never records an ACCEPTED status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE; the >= ACCEPTED guards in handlePreAccept and findPreAcceptConflicts therefore only ever see COMMITTED on non-leaders (S11-handleAccept, S9-handlePreAccept, S17-find-conflicts).

handlePrepareReply's sub-cases 3 and 4 carry textually identical guards, so sub-case 3 always wins and sub-case 4 never runs; bcastTryPreAccept is called only from sub-case 4, so handleTryPreAccept, findPreAcceptConflicts, handleTryPreAcceptReply and the possibleQuorum/deferMap machinery are unreachable dead code, and a recovery with weaker pre-accept support takes sub-case 5, which restarts phase 1 with the recovered value (a more conservative path) (S15-handlePrepareReply, S16-handleTryPreAccept, S17-find-conflicts, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply).

handleTryPreAcceptReply's defer-cycle guard counts lb.possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId] inside a loop over q, so the count can only be 0 or N and never equals N/2; the counting error has no reachable consequence because the handler is reachable only from the dead sub-case 4 (S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply).

recordInstanceMetadata writes bal and vbal into the same [0:4] byte range and stores Status at offset 4 inside a 9+4N header, and no reader of that format exists in the snapshot; the launcher always passes durable = false (S19-durable-record, S24-runReplica-epaxos).
the transconf branch inside Exec.strongconnect computes state.Conflict but performs no action, and run.go passes transconf = false (S20-exec, S24-runReplica-epaxos).

the N<=3 with Thrifty configuration skips the fast-path attribute-equality check while still committing at preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 = 1. The committed vector is the merge of the leader's own and the counted replies' (seq,deps) (mergeAttributes, installed into the bookkeeping before the branch choice), so the exemption does not publish the leader's own proposal vector; what it removes is the requirement that every counted reply already equal that merged vector, which is the step that otherwise either forces agreement or triggers the accept round that puts the merged vector on a majority. With exactly one counted peer the merged vector equals that peer's record in every compared component, and in an owner-led instance the peer skips precisely the leader's own row, so the fast quorum's two members both hold the committed vector at the same vbal. The residual exposure is therefore one component in a recovery-led phase 1 (leader != owner), where mergeAttributes ignores the leader's own row while the peer may hold a higher value for that row; that needs the peer to know more about the leader's own row than the leader does, which no read path establishes for a live leader (S7-attributes, S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply, S21-quorum-sizes).
before.rationale: Both core relationships are traced through real entry points (client propose to phase 1 to pre-accept replies to fast or slow decision to commit install, and ballot promise to nack-driven prepare to recovery sub-cases) and their connection is stated in terms of the per-instance record, the highest-vbal reply rule, the committed short-circuit and the ballot comparison that rejects old replies. The remaining questions are local anomalies inside handlers rather than missing formation, authority-transition or old-work handling, so the overview is recorded as usable with those anomalies kept as open_details and as the first Candidate's discriminator.

feedback.answered: The client-side half of the question is answered on sources: the captured client has no retry and no reply deadline. SendProposal writes each proposal once (to the leader, or to the closest replica in the leaderless EPaxos configuration of run.go) and never re-sends it (S29-client-sendproposal). The reply path is a blocking read: WaitReplies loops on GetReplyFrom(waitFrom) and only leaves the loop when the read returns an error such as net.ErrClosed, at which point it logs and stops rather than re-sending (S28-client-waitreplies, S30-client-getreplyfrom). There is no timeout, no outstanding-request table and no CommandId-based retransmission, so a proposal whose instance was committed as NOOP by a recovery is never completed on either side: the recovering replica never held the proposals (it preserves only its own record's clientProposals), the re-propose branch requires the commit to land on the committing replica's own row with a single NONE command (S13-handleCommit), and the client does not re-issue the request.
remaining: whether the replica side could be expected to complete another replica's proposal, i.e. whether the recovering replica should adopt the owner's proposals when it recovers the owner's row (no read path does)

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known. In the captured implementation the recovering replica also raises its own record's vbal to the newly made ballot before it builds its PrepareReply, so the resolution's running maximum starts above any value that other replicas accepted at older vbals; the direct checks for claim C1-recovery-adopts-committed-vector confirmed in scope that this lets a recovery commit a NOOP vector for an instance another replica already holds as COMMITTED with a real command, and that the recoverer's Commit broadcast does not repair the disagreement.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

open_details: handlePreAccept's status >= ACCEPTED branch stores the incoming command in InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler uses preAccept.Replica (S9-handlePreAccept). Source review of every status-advancing path found no state with Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil: acceptors keep Status NONE, the leader-side accept/commit paths copy commands, and the only nil-Cmds records are fresh defaults with Status NONE. The wrong-slot write is therefore unreachable while acceptors do not record acceptance; the unprotected premise is whether handleAccept is required to record ACCEPTED (S11-handleAccept, S12-handleAcceptReply, S13-handleCommit).

handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal but never records an ACCEPTED status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE; the >= ACCEPTED guards in handlePreAccept and findPreAcceptConflicts therefore only ever see COMMITTED on non-leaders (S11-handleAccept, S9-handlePreAccept, S17-find-conflicts).

handlePrepareReply's sub-cases 3 and 4 carry textually identical guards, so sub-case 3 always wins and sub-case 4 never runs; bcastTryPreAccept is called only from sub-case 4, so handleTryPreAccept, findPreAcceptConflicts, handleTryPreAcceptReply and the possibleQuorum/deferMap machinery are unreachable dead code, and a recovery with weaker pre-accept support takes sub-case 5, which restarts phase 1 with the recovered value (a more conservative path) (S15-handlePrepareReply, S16-handleTryPreAccept, S17-find-conflicts, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply).

handleTryPreAcceptReply's defer-cycle guard counts lb.possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId] inside a loop over q, so the count can only be 0 or N and never equals N/2; the counting error has no reachable consequence because the handler is reachable only from the dead sub-case 4 (S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply).

recordInstanceMetadata writes bal at [0:4) and then vbal into the same bytes, with Status at byte [4] and Seq at [5:9); the direct check for claim C2-durable-record-preserves-written-fields confirmed in scope that the produced record carries vbal at offset 0 and no bal value, so the ballot context the function writes is not recoverable from the layout. No reader of the format exists in the snapshot and run.go passes durable = false, so the consequence is bounded to any future or external reader (S19-durable-record, S24-runReplica-epaxos).
the transconf branch inside Exec.strongconnect computes state.Conflict but performs no action, and run.go passes transconf = false (S20-exec, S24-runReplica-epaxos).

the N<=3 with Thrifty configuration skips the fast-path attribute-equality check while still committing at preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 = 1. The committed vector is the merge of the leader's own and the counted replies' (seq,deps) (mergeAttributes, installed into the bookkeeping before the branch choice), so the exemption does not publish the leader's own proposal vector; what it removes is the requirement that every counted reply already equal that merged vector, which is the step that otherwise either forces agreement or triggers the accept round that puts the merged vector on a majority. With exactly one counted peer the merged vector equals that peer's record in every compared component, and in an owner-led instance the peer skips precisely the leader's own row, so the fast quorum's two members both hold the committed vector at the same vbal. The residual exposure is therefore one component in a recovery-led phase 1 (leader != owner), where mergeAttributes ignores the leader's own row while the peer may hold a higher value for that row; that needs the peer to know more about the leader's own row than the leader does, which no read path establishes for a live leader (S7-attributes, S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply, S21-quorum-sizes).
before.rationale: Both core relationships are traced through real entry points (client propose to phase 1 to pre-accept replies to fast or slow decision to commit install, and ballot promise to nack-driven prepare to recovery sub-cases) and their connection is stated in terms of the per-instance record, the highest-vbal reply rule, the committed short-circuit and the ballot comparison that rejects old replies. The remaining questions are local anomalies inside handlers rather than missing formation, authority-transition or old-work handling, so the overview is recorded as usable with those anomalies kept as open_details and as the first Candidate's discriminator.

The harness admits the operation with the real handlePropose and delivers the commit to the real handleCommit, and the local construction run reports COMMITTED with pending_after 0 and reproposed_on_channel 1; the trusted runner and a fresh correspondence review decide the formal outcome, which is expected to hold.

Pauses the client-completion Candidate with its two halves answered: the owner-alive half is a confirmed protection (claim C5) and the owner-gone half is a contract boundary in which no replica can complete the operation because proposals are never transmitted, while the driver client neither retries nor times out. What would reopen it is a client retry implementation, a replica-side proposal transfer, or a harness that drives the client library.

feedback.answered: The question is answered in two parts on sources. Where the owner survives and processes the NOOP commit, the admitted operation is kept alive: the reviewed check for claim C5 confirmed that the owner installs the commit and re-proposes the operation onto the propose channel (artifact fb1d0e558f4641c7850fe8aaca4068df: pending cleared, one proposal waiting). Where the owner is gone, no replica can complete the operation, because a proposal is never transmitted: handlePropose attaches the GPropose to the instance's local bookkeeping and recovery preserves only the recovering replica's own record's proposals, so the operation exists in no surviving process; the captured driver client sends each proposal once and then blocks on the reply stream with no timeout or retry, so nothing re-issues it either (S13-handleCommit, S8-handlePropose-startPhase1, S28-client-waitreplies, S29-client-sendproposal). The absence of an in-repository mechanism is therefore a contract boundary rather than an unnoticed replica bug: completion after the admitting replica is lost is owed to a client retry that this snapshot does not implement.

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known. In the captured implementation the recovering replica also raises its own record's vbal to the newly made ballot before it builds its PrepareReply, so the resolution's running maximum starts above any value that other replicas accepted at older vbals; the direct checks for claim C1-recovery-adopts-committed-vector confirmed in scope that this lets a recovery commit a NOOP vector for an instance another replica already holds as COMMITTED with a real command, and that the recoverer's Commit broadcast does not repair the disagreement.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo.

open_details: handlePreAccept's status >= ACCEPTED branch stores the incoming command in InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler uses preAccept.Replica (S9-handlePreAccept). Source review of every status-advancing path found no state with Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil: acceptors keep Status NONE, the leader-side accept/commit paths copy commands, and the only nil-Cmds records are fresh defaults with Status NONE. The wrong-slot write is therefore unreachable while acceptors do not record acceptance; the unprotected premise is whether handleAccept is required to record ACCEPTED (S11-handleAccept, S12-handleAcceptReply, S13-handleCommit).

handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal but never records an ACCEPTED status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE; the >= ACCEPTED guards in handlePreAccept and findPreAcceptConflicts therefore only ever see COMMITTED on non-leaders (S11-handleAccept, S9-handlePreAccept, S17-find-conflicts).

handlePrepareReply's sub-cases 3 and 4 carry textually identical guards, so sub-case 3 always wins and sub-case 4 never runs; bcastTryPreAccept is called only from sub-case 4, so handleTryPreAccept, findPreAcceptConflicts, handleTryPreAcceptReply and the possibleQuorum/deferMap machinery are unreachable dead code, and a recovery with weaker pre-accept support takes sub-case 5, which restarts phase 1 with the recovered value (a more conservative path) (S15-handlePrepareReply, S16-handleTryPreAccept, S17-find-conflicts, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply).

handleTryPreAcceptReply's defer-cycle guard counts lb.possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId] inside a loop over q, so the count can only be 0 or N and never equals N/2; the counting error has no reachable consequence because the handler is reachable only from the dead sub-case 4 (S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply).

recordInstanceMetadata writes bal at [0:4) and then vbal into the same bytes, with Status at byte [4] and Seq at [5:9); the direct check for claim C2-durable-record-preserves-written-fields confirmed in scope that the produced record carries vbal at offset 0 and no bal value, so the ballot context the function writes is not recoverable from the layout. No reader of the format exists in the snapshot and run.go passes durable = false, so the consequence is bounded to any future or external reader (S19-durable-record, S24-runReplica-epaxos).
the transconf branch inside Exec.strongconnect computes state.Conflict but performs no action, and run.go passes transconf = false (S20-exec, S24-runReplica-epaxos).

the N<=3 with Thrifty configuration skips the fast-path attribute-equality check while still committing at preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 = 1. The committed vector is the merge of the leader's own and the counted replies' (seq,deps) (mergeAttributes, installed into the bookkeeping before the branch choice), so the exemption does not publish the leader's own proposal vector; what it removes is the requirement that every counted reply already equal that merged vector, which is the step that otherwise either forces agreement or triggers the accept round that puts the merged vector on a majority. With exactly one counted peer the merged vector equals that peer's record in every compared component, and in an owner-led instance the peer skips precisely the leader's own row, so the fast quorum's two members both hold the committed vector at the same vbal. The residual exposure is therefore one component in a recovery-led phase 1 (leader != owner), where mergeAttributes ignores the leader's own row while the peer may hold a higher value for that row; that needs the peer to know more about the leader's own row than the leader does, which no read path establishes for a live leader (S7-attributes, S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply, S21-quorum-sizes).

handleCommit's NOOP re-proposal branch dereferences leader bookkeeping that message-created records do not have, so a legal NOOP commit for an instance the replica owns terminates the handler; the direct check for claim C4-noop-commit-without-bookkeeping confirmed in scope that a record created by a recovery-led PreAccept plus the commit raises a nil pointer dereference and leaves the instance uncommitted. The run loop has no recover, so the panic is inferred to end the process; the history that leaves a restarted owner in that state and the client-side consequence of the same NOOP recovery remain unread (S13-handleCommit, S9-handlePreAccept, S3-run-dispatch).

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known. In the captured implementation the recovering replica also raises its own record's vbal to the newly made ballot before it builds its PrepareReply, so the resolution's running maximum starts above any value that other replicas accepted at older vbals; the direct checks for claim C1-recovery-adopts-committed-vector confirmed in scope that this lets a recovery commit a NOOP vector for an instance another replica already holds as COMMITTED with a real command, and that the recoverer's Commit broadcast does not repair the disagreement. The same masking holds when the recovering replica is the replica the deployment promoted to leader (IsLeader true, so makeBallot raises the new ballot past maxRecvBallot): the promoted-variant check for claim C6-recovery-ignores-committed-reply-when-promoted confirmed in scope that the committed reply is still skipped and the NOOP vector committed, and the accept handler's own rejection branch for a higher-ballot AcceptReply is unreachable because the ballot-equality gate returns first (claim C7-accept-reply-higher-ballot-is-a-rejection, confirmed in scope), so a rejected round waits for the timeout-driven recovery.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo. Progress when a round is rejected does not come from the handlers: the direct check for claim C8-timeout-enqueues-blocked-instance confirmed that the executor's per-row timeout enqueues the blocked instance for recovery after roughly twelve seconds of wall clock, so a stalled row is recovered by the timeout path rather than by a rejection signal.

open_details: handlePreAccept's status >= ACCEPTED branch stores the incoming command in InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler uses preAccept.Replica (S9-handlePreAccept). Source review of every status-advancing path found no state with Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil: acceptors keep Status NONE, the leader-side accept/commit paths copy commands, and the only nil-Cmds records are fresh defaults with Status NONE. The wrong-slot write is therefore unreachable while acceptors do not record acceptance; the unprotected premise is whether handleAccept is required to record ACCEPTED (S11-handleAccept, S12-handleAcceptReply, S13-handleCommit).

handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal but never records an ACCEPTED status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE; the >= ACCEPTED guards in handlePreAccept and findPreAcceptConflicts therefore only ever see COMMITTED on non-leaders (S11-handleAccept, S9-handlePreAccept, S17-find-conflicts).

handlePrepareReply's sub-cases 3 and 4 carry textually identical guards, so sub-case 3 always wins and sub-case 4 never runs; bcastTryPreAccept is called only from sub-case 4, so handleTryPreAccept, findPreAcceptConflicts, handleTryPreAcceptReply and the possibleQuorum/deferMap machinery are unreachable dead code, and a recovery with weaker pre-accept support takes sub-case 5, which restarts phase 1 with the recovered value (a more conservative path) (S15-handlePrepareReply, S16-handleTryPreAccept, S17-find-conflicts, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply).

handleTryPreAcceptReply's defer-cycle guard counts lb.possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId] inside a loop over q, so the count can only be 0 or N and never equals N/2; the counting error has no reachable consequence because the handler is reachable only from the dead sub-case 4 (S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply).

recordInstanceMetadata writes bal at [0:4) and then vbal into the same bytes, with Status at byte [4] and Seq at [5:9); the direct check for claim C2-durable-record-preserves-written-fields confirmed in scope that the produced record carries vbal at offset 0 and no bal value, so the ballot context the function writes is not recoverable from the layout. No reader of the format exists in the snapshot and run.go passes durable = false, so the consequence is bounded to any future or external reader (S19-durable-record, S24-runReplica-epaxos).
the transconf branch inside Exec.strongconnect computes state.Conflict but performs no action, and run.go passes transconf = false (S20-exec, S24-runReplica-epaxos).

the N<=3 with Thrifty configuration skips the fast-path attribute-equality check while still committing at preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 = 1. The committed vector is the merge of the leader's own and the counted replies' (seq,deps) (mergeAttributes, installed into the bookkeeping before the branch choice), so the exemption does not publish the leader's own proposal vector; what it removes is the requirement that every counted reply already equal that merged vector, which is the step that otherwise either forces agreement or triggers the accept round that puts the merged vector on a majority. With exactly one counted peer the merged vector equals that peer's record in every compared component, and in an owner-led instance the peer skips precisely the leader's own row, so the fast quorum's two members both hold the committed vector at the same vbal. The residual exposure is therefore one component in a recovery-led phase 1 (leader != owner), where mergeAttributes ignores the leader's own row while the peer may hold a higher value for that row; that needs the peer to know more about the leader's own row than the leader does, which no read path establishes for a live leader (S7-attributes, S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply, S21-quorum-sizes).

handleCommit's NOOP re-proposal branch dereferences leader bookkeeping that message-created records do not have, so a legal NOOP commit for an instance the replica owns terminates the handler; the direct check for claim C4-noop-commit-without-bookkeeping confirmed in scope that a record created by a recovery-led PreAccept plus the commit raises a nil pointer dereference and leaves the instance uncommitted. The run loop has no recover, so the panic is inferred to end the process; the history that leaves a restarted owner in that state and the client-side consequence of the same NOOP recovery remain unread (S13-handleCommit, S9-handlePreAccept, S3-run-dispatch).

handleAcceptReply returns whenever a reply's ballot differs from the round's, so the nack branch behind that gate never runs and a peer that answers with a higher ballot is ignored rather than counted as a rejection; the direct check for claim C7 confirmed nacks 0 and no reaction, and the pre-accept side has no rejection signal either (PreAcceptReply copies the request's ballot and handlePreAccept returns silently for a smaller ballot), so progress after a rejection depends on the 10s execution timeout rather than on the handlers (S12-handleAcceptReply, S11-handleAccept, S4-execute-loop).

with recording enabled, the phase-1 entry records metadata through the recovering replica's own row while installing the instance under the owner's row, so a recovery-led phase 1 either records a different instance's ballot context or terminates on an absent record; the direct check for claim C9-durable-recorder-uses-the-instance-row confirmed the nil dereference with Durable true and an empty own row, and the case where that slot exists is still unread (S8-handlePropose-startPhase1, S19-durable-record).
after.rationale: Both core relationships are traced through real entry points (client propose to phase 1 to pre-accept replies to fast or slow decision to commit install, and ballot promise to nack-driven prepare to recovery sub-cases) and their connection is stated in terms of the per-instance record, the highest-vbal reply rule, the committed short-circuit and the ballot comparison that rejects old replies. The remaining questions are local anomalies inside handlers rather than missing formation, authority-transition or old-work handling, so the overview is recorded as usable with those anomalies kept as open_details and as the first Candidate's discriminator.

Records a new locally reproduced finding (the command value length is truncated on the wire for values beyond the two-byte field) plus the exact framing constraint that blocked filing it as a check this turn. Adds the codec and configuration sources; no map object changes.

feedback.answered: A codec contract break is reproduced locally: the value codec frames a command's value length in two bytes on both sides, while the client's command size is configuration-driven (aws.conf sets 1000, and the field allows up to 65535). A 70000-byte value marshals to 70013 bytes but unmarshals as 4464 bytes with only 4477 bytes consumed, so the value is silently shortened and the remaining 65536 bytes stay in the stream, shifting every following message boundary on that reader. The finding is construction knowledge: the harness is written and runs (explore_value_len_test.go) but the formal check could not be filed yet because the question framing that references the codec's sources did not satisfy the validator's requirement that the selected behavior and principal fact carry an A1 or A2 relationship to the codec's material.
remaining: reshaping that question so its principal fact and selected behavior are the ones the map attributes to command framing (or accepting the codec material as a supporting-layer question with an explicit A1/A2 link), then filing the check
whether the client library caps the command size it builds, which was not read in that detail
what a replica reader does on the following message once the stream is shifted
feedback.rationale: The observation is worth retaining even without the formal check, and the validator constraint is recorded precisely so the next attempt frames it correctly instead of iterating blindly. The default deployment is inside the field's range, so the finding's importance is bounded to configurations whose command size exceeds 65535 bytes.

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

The wrong-slot write is therefore unreachable while acceptors do not record acceptance; the unprotected premise is whether handleAccept is required to record ACCEPTED (S11-handleAccept, S12-handleAcceptReply, S13-handleCommit).

handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal but never records an ACCEPTED status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE; the >= ACCEPTED guards in handlePreAccept and findPreAcceptConflicts therefore only ever see COMMITTED on non-leaders (S11-handleAccept, S9-handlePreAccept, S17-find-conflicts).

handlePrepareReply's sub-cases 3 and 4 carry textually identical guards, so sub-case 3 always wins and sub-case 4 never runs; bcastTryPreAccept is called only from sub-case 4, so handleTryPreAccept, findPreAcceptConflicts, handleTryPreAcceptReply and the possibleQuorum/deferMap machinery are unreachable dead code, and a recovery with weaker pre-accept support takes sub-case 5, which restarts phase 1 with the recovered value (a more conservative path) (S15-handlePrepareReply, S16-handleTryPreAccept, S17-find-conflicts, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply).

handleTryPreAcceptReply's defer-cycle guard counts lb.possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId] inside a loop over q, so the count can only be 0 or N and never equals N/2; the counting error has no reachable consequence because the handler is reachable only from the dead sub-case 4 (S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply).

recordInstanceMetadata writes bal at [0:4) and then vbal into the same bytes, with Status at byte [4] and Seq at [5:9); the direct check for claim C2-durable-record-preserves-written-fields confirmed in scope that the produced record carries vbal at offset 0 and no bal value, so the ballot context the function writes is not recoverable from the layout. No reader of the format exists in the snapshot and run.go passes durable = false, so the consequence is bounded to any future or external reader (S19-durable-record, S24-runReplica-epaxos).
the transconf branch inside Exec.strongconnect computes state.Conflict but performs no action, and run.go passes transconf = false (S20-exec, S24-runReplica-epaxos).

the N<=3 with Thrifty configuration skips the fast-path attribute-equality check while still committing at preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 = 1. The committed vector is the merge of the leader's own and the counted replies' (seq,deps) (mergeAttributes, installed into the bookkeeping before the branch choice), so the exemption does not publish the leader's own proposal vector; what it removes is the requirement that every counted reply already equal that merged vector, which is the step that otherwise either forces agreement or triggers the accept round that puts the merged vector on a majority. With exactly one counted peer the merged vector equals that peer's record in every compared component, and in an owner-led instance the peer skips precisely the leader's own row, so the fast quorum's two members both hold the committed vector at the same vbal. The residual exposure is therefore one component in a recovery-led phase 1 (leader != owner), where mergeAttributes ignores the leader's own row while the peer may hold a higher value for that row; that needs the peer to know more about the leader's own row than the leader does, which no read path establishes for a live leader (S7-attributes, S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply, S21-quorum-sizes).

handleCommit's NOOP re-proposal branch dereferences leader bookkeeping that message-created records do not have, so a legal NOOP commit for an instance the replica owns terminates the handler; the direct check for claim C4-noop-commit-without-bookkeeping confirmed in scope that a record created by a recovery-led PreAccept plus the commit raises a nil pointer dereference and leaves the instance uncommitted. The run loop has no recover, so the panic is inferred to end the process; the history that leaves a restarted owner in that state and the client-side consequence of the same NOOP recovery remain unread (S13-handleCommit, S9-handlePreAccept, S3-run-dispatch).

handleAcceptReply returns whenever a reply's ballot differs from the round's, so the nack branch behind that gate never runs and a peer that answers with a higher ballot is ignored rather than counted as a rejection; the direct check for claim C7 confirmed nacks 0 and no reaction, and the pre-accept side has no rejection signal either (PreAcceptReply copies the request's ballot and handlePreAccept returns silently for a smaller ballot), so progress after a rejection depends on the 10s execution timeout rather than on the handlers (S12-handleAcceptReply, S11-handleAccept, S4-execute-loop).

with recording enabled, the phase-1 entry records metadata through the recovering replica's own row while installing the instance under the owner's row, so a recovery-led phase 1 either records a different instance's ballot context or terminates on an absent record; the direct check for claim C9-durable-recorder-uses-the-instance-row confirmed the nil dereference with Durable true and an empty own row, and the case where that slot exists is still unread (S8-handlePropose-startPhase1, S19-durable-record).

the command value codec frames a value's length in a two-byte field on both sides, while the client's command size is configuration-driven; the direct check for claim C10-command-value-length-survives-the-wire confirmed that a 70000-byte value is written as 70013 bytes but decoded as 4464 bytes with only 4477 bytes consumed, so the value is shortened and the rest of the stream is left for the next message. The default configuration's 1000-byte commands never reach the boundary, and what a replica reader does with the shifted stream is unread (S37-state-value-codec, S38-client-command-size).
after.rationale: Both core relationships are traced through real entry points (client propose to phase 1 to pre-accept replies to fast or slow decision to commit install, and ballot promise to nack-driven prepare to recovery sub-cases) and their connection is stated in terms of the per-instance record, the highest-vbal reply rule, the committed short-circuit and the ballot comparison that rejects old replies. The remaining questions are local anomalies inside handlers rather than missing formation, authority-transition or old-work handling, so the overview is recorded as usable with those anomalies kept as open_details and as the first Candidate's discriminator.

after.reason: the value and command wire codecs frame every command a replica sends or receives; they carry no protocol decision, but the direct check for claim C10-command-value-length-survives-the-wire confirmed that a value beyond the two-byte length field is silently shortened while its bytes remain in the stream, which the default 1000-byte command size does not reach (S37-state-value-codec, S38-client-command-size).

selections.rationale: Second scenario for the same obligation, covering the consequence the first check left open: the leftover bytes of a truncated value shift the stream, so the next command in the same buffer decodes to garbage. The harness writes a 70000-byte value followed by a small command and decodes both in order; the local construction run shows the second command with op 197, an arbitrary key and a 53198-byte value, with 12341 bytes remaining, so the trust the codec places in the length field destroys the following command as well. The trusted runner and a fresh correspondence review decide the formal outcome.

Semantic review of the second scenario for C10-command-value-length-survives-the-wire (artifact 1f094469…, executed as 8628f4fc…). The item assesses requirement versus predicate, the concatenation premise, the oracle, identity, and the bounded consequences.

F2 scope clarification on the accepted C1 unit, using the C3 claim and its reviewed check as the new basis, so the attribution the superseded artifact blurred is stated in the claim itself. The obligation, its sources, conditions and artifacts are unchanged; only the scope text gains the boundary and names C3.

Re-execution of the C1 check against the current claim version. The F2 scope clarification amended the claim's scope text (naming C3 for the applied-state proposition) without changing the obligation, its sources or its conditions, but the framework requires new execution when a direct check's semantic inputs change, so the three-property plan is submitted again: adoption at the resolution, the recoverer-versus-committed-peer comparison and agreement across replicas after the Commit broadcast. The harness bytes are the reviewed driven version, and the earlier artifacts' observations are unchanged; what is needed is a fresh execution bound to claim version 2 plus a current-version correspondence review.

Direct oracle correspondence remains disputed: Requirement versus predicate: the accepted claim requires that a reply reporting the instance COMMITTED be adopted; the added property instead asserts that, after each replica applies the instance it holds committed, the state machines agree on the instance's key. The observation is a consequence of the requirement rather than the requirement's own premise, and the accepted claim's scope list names exactly that consequence as excluded (execution of the instance and client-visible replies). Entry and observation: the harness applies each record with Exec.executeCommand directly and probes the store with a GET command, which is a declared substitution (the production executeCommands loop, watermark advancement and the recovery timeout are not exercised); the records' COMMITTED status is by construction, and the three values printed in the event are read from the replicated store rather than derived from a context expected to change. Oracle and identity: comparing the three printed values for one instance and one key is a fair encoding of applied-state agreement, and the instance identity is shared with the prerequisite reply, so the failure is not an artefact of correlation. Contrary evidence and the reason for the negative judgment: the element that conflicts is the claim's own excluded list, which the source of record for the accepted obligation states; a consequence outside that scope can still be true and valuable, but confirming it under this claim would treat an independent limit as a confirmation gate, so the artifact should either drop the applied-state property or the proposition should be fixed as its own obligation whose scope includes applying the instance to the state machine. The rest of the artifact (the correction that drives every queued round and re-reads InstanceSpace) reproduces the earlier reviewed findings and does not itself change them.

items.rationale: Requirement versus predicate: the accepted claim is that a slow-quorum reply reporting the instance COMMITTED must be adopted; the plan's observable property asserts adopted_committed on the resolution event, and the harness prints instance_status and command_after in the same event, so the assertion is checkable against the raw fields rather than only through the derived boolean. Entry and caller duties: the recovery is entered directly through startRecoveryForInstance instead of the executeCommands timeout, and the peer's COMMITTED record is prepared rather than produced by a proposal and commit round; both substitutions are declared in the claim's scope and in the harness legality, and neither is needed for the resolution step the claim is about, because the resolution reads only the record, the reply slice and the running ballot. Oracle: adopted_committed is computed by the harness as an OR of two status fields, and the same event carries the status the code actually stored, so a change in the protocol's status semantics would show up in instance_status as well. Identity: the prerequisite and the resolution event share instance 1.0, which is the instance the harness seeds and drives, so correlation is non-trivial and monotone; the identity is written by the harness rather than read from the record, which is noted as a limitation rather than a defect because the harness constructs exactly one instance. Legal history: the prepared COMMITTED record corresponds to a state some history produced, but the trigger path is substituted, so the item is scoped to the resolution decision. Observation path and completion: all handlers are synchronous in the harness, the resolution is observed after handlePrepareReply returns, and the emitted message code is retained, so no wait or join is implied. Counterevidence: the alternative reading (the local record's new ballot legitimately outranks an older committed vbal) is recorded in the claim grounding and is not settled by this check; the item therefore does not promote the finding beyond the reviewed correspondence of predicate and observation. Contrary evidence and alternatives: the two reservations I hold are explained rather than hidden. First, the trigger (executeCommands timeout) and the production of the committed record are substituted, which limits the claim to the resolution decision; second, an alternative reading is that a recovering replica is only required to adopt the value with the highest vbal and that its own newly made ballot legitimately outranks an older committed ballot. I judge the alternative untenable because vbal records the ballot at which a value was accepted, while the recovering replica's fresh ballot carries no accepted value, and because the ignored reply reports COMMITTED, which is the one status the protocol treats as final; the check therefore corresponds to the written obligation, and the reservation is recorded so a later review can challenge it on sources rather than being surprised by it.
